issues.issue: SW fetch handler creates un-revalidated cache-first entries for any same-origin GET not in SHELL, so a file that is added later (or forgotten in SHELL) is served stale forever after every subsequent deploy. Hits the 'serve a stale app after deploy' criterion.
issues.evidence: pwa_and_mobile / sw.js: "Same-origin shell URL → respond from cache immediately...; if not cached → network then cache." and "revalidateShell(): Fetch every SHELL URL with {cache:'no-cache'}... compare each ETag". Only SHELL-listed URLs are ever revalidated, but the opportunistic branch caches any same-origin GET (a new src/views/*.js module, a new data file, a new icon) the first time it is fetched online. From then on it is cache-first with no ETag check, so after the next deploy the page runs new app.js against the old copy of that module until someone bumps CACHE (the design says CACHE is 'bumped only when SW logic changes'). CLAUDE.md invariants (file_layout) say nothing about maintaining SHELL, and no test lints SHELL against the src/ and data/ tree, so the omission is likely over the app's life. The same gap makes cache.addAll(SHELL) fail silently (no install, no offline) if any listed path 404s.
issues.fix: (1) In the fetch handler, apply cache-first only to URLs that are in the SHELL set; for any other same-origin GET use network-first with cache fallback (or stale-while-revalidate per request: respond from cache and refetch with cache:'no-cache', cache.put the fresh response). (2) Add test/sw.test.js that parses SHELL out of sw.js and asserts it equals the set of index.html, style.css, config.js, manifest, every src/**/*.js, every data/*.json and every icon on disk (both directions). (3) Add to CLAUDE.md: 'new src/data/icon file ⇒ add it to SHELL in sw.js (the test will fail otherwise)'. (4) Have the page log/console-warn when navigator.serviceWorker.register rejects or when the SW posts an install-failed message, so a 404 in SHELL is visible during the browser checklist.

issues.issue: Profile switching on a shared phone can write one user's set.logged events into the other user's partition with a foreign sessionId: settings.activeSessionId is a single per-phone value, makeEvent stamps user = settings.user at dispatch time, and nothing blocks 'Switch user' while a session is active. This meets the 'one user's events corrupt the other's state' criterion.
issues.evidence: storage_and_sync.local: "Both users can exist on one phone (events carry user); Settings → Switch user changes settings.user only." rendering_and_state: "dispatch(type, data): makeEvent (id, ts, day, dev, user=me...)" and "a reload mid-workout lands back on #/session/:id via settings.activeSessionId". Scenario: Sean starts session S on his phone, Cat's phone is dead so she switches the profile to Cat mid-session; the router restores #/session/S from settings.activeSessionId, every DONE tap emits set.logged{sessionId:S, user:'cat'} into log/cat/<seanDev>/. reduce() partitions by user, so Cat's partition now contains sets for a session whose session.started lives in Sean's partition: depending on reducer tolerance this is an orphan session with targetsPrescribed=0 (division in targets_hit_pct), XP perSetDone credited to Cat for Sean's sets (scoreboard 'xp' category polluted), or a throw. Sean's state also loses those sets. Related: history.js 'edit via sheet (emits new set.logged)' must be impossible for partner sessions (partner is 'read-only' by intent but no guard or test is named).
issues.fix: Make activeSessionId per user (settings.activeSession = {sean: id|null, cat: id|null}) and have the router restore only users[me]'s session; refuse 'Switch user' while a session for the current user is open (offer Finish/Abandon first); in dispatch(), validate that any event carrying sessionId refers to a session in users[me].sessions (reject otherwise) and that History/Duo never render data-action edit controls for the partner's sessions; in reduce(), drop (and count) set.logged whose sessionId is unknown in that user's partition rather than creating a stub. Add a reduce.test.js case: 'set.logged with user=cat and Sean's sessionId never changes Cat's XP/targets and never touches Sean's session'.

issues.issue: The CSP meta in index.html blocks two things the Session screen relies on: the base64 WAV rest-timer beep (media-src falls back to default-src 'self', which does not include data:) and any style="..." attribute produced by the innerHTML-rendered html`` templates (style-src 'self' forbids inline style attributes). The one-tap flow still logs, but the rest timer beep, XP/level bar widths, boss-battle bar and rest ring will fail silently.
issues.evidence: file_layout index.html: "CSP meta (default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self')". pwa_and_mobile: "beeps via a short base64 WAV (unlocked by the DONE gesture)"; rendering_and_state: "each view is (state) => html string...; root.innerHTML replaced"; views: "XP/level bar", "active boss battle bar (combined vs target)", "rest timer ring". Per CSP3, `data:` URLs are only allowed by a directive that lists data:, and inline style attributes require 'unsafe-inline' or a hash on style-src; CSSOM writes (el.style.width=...) are allowed but setAttribute('style') and style= in markup are not.
issues.fix: Either add `media-src 'self' data:` or, better, ship icons/beep.wav (add it to SHELL) or synthesise the beep with a WebAudio oscillator (AudioContext created+resumed synchronously inside the DONE click handler, before the `await store.append`, so iOS keeps it unlocked). For dynamic sizes, either use presentation attributes/SVG attributes (width=, stroke-dasharray=, data-pct + a CSS custom property set via el.style.setProperty after render) or add `'unsafe-inline'` to style-src (acceptable here because all user text is escaped and the token is never in the DOM). Add a browser-checklist step: no CSP violations in the console after one full session.

issues.issue: Setup-then-install ordering on iOS: the app boots into #/setup and defers the Add-to-Home-Screen tip, but iOS gives a home-screen web app its own storage partition, so a profile, placement quiz, dev id and pasted token entered in the Safari tab are absent in the installed app (and vice versa).
issues.evidence: file_layout setup.js: onboarding runs first, 'token paste is deferred to Settings'; pwa_and_mobile: "iOS: Add to Home Screen instructions shown once when display-mode standalone is not matched" (i.e. after the setup flow). WebKit blog (Full Third-Party Cookie Blocking and More): home-screen web apps 'are not part of Safari and thus have their own counter of days of use' — separate storage. Sessions logged from the Safari partition are pushed under log/<user>/<safariDev>/ and are recovered by the installed app as 'own user's other device' (read-only), so this is not data loss for synced events, but the token, settings, quiz and any local-only body metrics must be redone, and the user now has two dev ids for one phone.
issues.fix: On iOS Safari (not standalone), show an 'Install first' interstitial BEFORE setup with the Share → Add to Home Screen steps and a 'continue in browser anyway' link; keep the one-time tip for later. Keep deploy steps 12/13 as written (install before setup) and say why in README. Optionally let Settings → Export/Import carry settings (minus token) so a Safari-partition setup can be moved.

issues.issue: Pull-triggered full render() during an active session destroys the open bottom sheet's uncontrolled inputs and the DONE/undo affordance mid-tap; pulls run on every visibilitychange→visible and after every push, and the phone is backgrounded constantly during a workout (music, timer).
issues.evidence: storage_and_sync.sync_algorithm PULL step 4: "Recompute... render; toast"; TRIGGERS: "pull on ... visibilitychange→visible ... and after every successful push. Push on ... visibilitychange→hidden"; rendering_and_state: "root.innerHTML replaced ...; text inputs are uncontrolled and read on submit". So hide→push→show→pull→render happens on every screen wake; if the reps/RPE sheet was open its typed values are lost.
issues.fix: In app.js, when ui.route is #/session/* or ui.sheet is open, have pull() update state.users[partner]/state.duo only and mark ui.dirtyPartner=true; re-render on the next dispatch() or route change (the Session screen never shows partner data). Also treat pull-to-refresh and the Today/Duo screens as the only places a pull may re-render synchronously.

issues.issue: One-tap DONE can double-fire: the design names a delegated 'pointerup/click' listener; wiring both (or pointerup plus the synthesized click) logs set N and then set N+1 from one tap, since the DONE button's data-setIndex advances after each render.
issues.evidence: rendering_and_state: "one delegated pointerup/click listener on #app reads data-action / data-* attributes". With touch-action:manipulation there is no 300 ms delay, so click alone is sufficient; pointerup fires before click on the same tap.
issues.fix: Use a single `click` listener. In the session view, ignore a DONE for (sessionId, ladder, setIndex) if an identical done:true set.logged was dispatched in the last 500 ms, and disable the button (aria-disabled) until the awaited IDB put resolves. Add a test: two DONE actions within 100 ms produce one set.logged.

issues.issue: Frozen plan inside session.started carries cues/stopIf/why/unlockHint strings, making that event ~3–6 KB instead of ~150 B; the monthly file and every PUT body grow to roughly 250–350 KB, which makes the iOS visibilitychange→hidden PUT more likely to be killed mid-upload (iOS gives a backgrounded page only a few seconds, and fetch keepalive is capped at 64 KB so it cannot be used).
issues.evidence: data_model: "~150 B/event × ~600 events/month ≈ 90 KB" versus progression_engine Plan shape frozen into session.started: per item 'name, cues:[...], stopIf:'...', ... why:'...', unlockHint:'...''. sync_algorithm PUSH step 2 re-uploads ALL local events for the partition every time. offline_queue relies on 'flush also runs on every foreground' to recover, and 409 recovery handles a lost response, so this is not data loss, but it is avoidable weight on the slowest path.
issues.fix: Freeze only what reproducibility needs: {workoutId, phaseId, weekIndex, deload, testDay, estMinutes, blocks:[{kind, items:[{ladder, stepId, exerciseId, load, sets:[{setIndex,targetReps|targetSec|targetRounds,restSec}], repsRange}]}]}; resolve name/cues/stopIf/why/unlockHint from spec at render time (fallback text if a stepId no longer exists). Add a program.test.js/reduce.test.js assertion that a serialized session.started is < 1.5 KB. Also add `pagehide` alongside visibilitychange as a push trigger (iOS fires pagehide more reliably) and keep session.finished as the primary immediate push.

issues.issue: The Settings token test reports 'write' from repo.permissions.push, which reflects SJJ363's org-owner permission on the repo, not the token's Contents grant; a fine-grained token created with Contents:Read only passes the test and fails on the first PUT.
issues.evidence: storage_and_sync.sync_algorithm TOKEN TEST: "GET /repos/{O}/{R} → 200 and permissions.push===true ... show 'Connected as <login> · write ...'". Fine-grained PATs do not expose granted permissions in response headers; the repository object's permissions block describes the authenticated user's role.
issues.fix: Label the test result 'repo reachable · data branch OK' and verify write on the first real PUT, mapping 403 'Resource not accessible by personal access token' to tokenState='invalid' with the hint 'token needs Contents: Read and write' (the 401/403 branch already exists); or perform a probe write to log/<user>/<dev>/.probe once and delete it (costs two commits; not recommended).

issues.issue: Turning syncMetrics off does not remove metrics-<yyyy-mm>.jsonl already pushed to the public data branch; the Body screen promises 'stays on this phone' and the opt-in is reversible in the UI but not in effect.
issues.evidence: storage_and_sync.remote: "Optional log/<user>/<dev>/metrics-<yyyy-mm>.jsonl only when syncMetrics is on"; body.js: "explicit 'stays on this phone' notice and the syncMetrics opt-in link". Body metrics are within the token's scope (Contents read/write), so this is not a scope leak, but it is a privacy expectation the design creates and does not honour.
issues.fix: When syncMetrics is switched off, offer 'Also delete metrics files from GitHub' which issues DELETE /repos/{O}/{R}/contents/{path} with the stored sha for each metrics-*.jsonl this device wrote (then note that git history still holds them and that a force-push from the laptop would be needed to purge). Word the opt-in as 'publishes to the public repo; removable from the branch tip, not from history'.

issues.issue: Minor doc inaccuracies to correct before writing README/CLAUDE.md: (a) fine-grained PATs no longer cap at 366 days — GitHub now allows no-expiration tokens unless an org policy blocks it; (b) 'at most one stale launch per deploy' is really 'at most one stale launch after the Pages CDN converges (≤10 min)'; (c) `mkdir log` in the orphan-branch step commits nothing (git ignores empty dirs) — harmless because the Contents API creates paths; (d) GitHub asks for ≥1 s between consecutive content-creating requests to avoid secondary limits, which matters on a month rollover when two files are PUT in one flush.
issues.evidence: docs.github.com managing-your-personal-access-tokens, Expiration step: "Infinite lifetimes are allowed but may be blocked by a maximum lifetime policy set by your organization or enterprise owner." Design token_handling: "Custom → 366 days (the maximum)". docs.github.com best-practices: "If you are making a large number of POST, PATCH, PUT, or DELETE requests, wait at least one second between each request." pwa_and_mobile: "Guarantee: at most one stale launch per deploy" vs "Residual staleness is the Pages CDN's own max-age=600".
issues.fix: (a) Offer 'No expiration' as the default in README and keep the expiry-nag field optional. (b) State the guarantee as 'one stale launch after CDN convergence'. (c) Drop `mkdir log` or add log/.gitkeep. (d) In sync.js sleep 1 s between consecutive PUTs within one flush.

summary: Verified against the docs: the Contents API claims hold (PUT returns 200/201/404/409/422; author.name+email both required and committer defaults to the token owner; raw media type valid to 100 MB; sha required for updates), git/trees accepts a branch name and returns per-blob shas, 304s to correctly authorised conditional requests are free against the primary limit, secondary limits are 80/min and 500/h content-creating, fine-grained PATs can target an org as resource owner with automatic approval for org owners, legacy Pages builds fire only on pushes to the source branch (so the orphan data branch never rebuilds the site), and WebKit exempts home-screen web apps from the 7-day script-writable-storage cap. The spine (IDB event log awaited before UI, sole-writer per (user,dev,month) files, union-by-id merge, pure reduce/engine/gamify/duo, relative URLs + hash routes at basePath '/') is sound for the mobile PWA lens. Refuted on three concrete correctness holes that must be fixed before use: (1) the SW opportunistically caches any same-origin GET outside SHELL and never revalidates it, so a new or unlisted module is served stale forever after later deploys (fix: cache-first only for SHELL, network-first elsewhere, plus a test that SHELL equals the file tree); (2) a single per-phone activeSessionId plus user stamped at dispatch time lets a mid-session 'Switch user' write Sean's sets into Cat's partition (fix: per-user activeSessionId, block switch during an open session, reject events whose sessionId is not in users[me]); (3) the CSP meta blocks the data: WAV beep and inline style attributes the rendered bars/ring rely on (fix: media-src data: or a file/WebAudio beep, and attribute/CSSOM-driven sizing or 'unsafe-inline' for style-src). Secondary: install-before-setup on iOS because the home-screen app has its own storage partition; pulls must not full-render during a session; use a single click listener with an idempotency guard for DONE; slim the frozen plan to ids/targets; label the token test honestly; make the metrics opt-out actually delete remote files; small doc corrections (no-expiration PATs now allowed, 1 s between PUTs).
